text: The line graph illustrates how many people visited three national parks, Redrock, Pinewood and Silverlake, over a twenty-year period from 2002 to 2022.

Overall, Redrock saw a dramatic increase in visitor numbers and went from being the least visited park to the most popular one. Pinewood, by contrast, remained broadly stable, whereas Silverlake experienced a gradual decline.

In 2002, Redrock attracted 1.2 million visitors, the lowest figure of the three. This number rose steadily to 1.7 million in 2010, overtaking Silverlake, and then climbed sharply, reaching 4.2 million by 2022. This was three and a half times the figure at the start of the period.

Pinewood, meanwhile, was the most visited park for most of the period, with numbers fluctuating slightly around 3 million. However, Redrock had overtaken it by 2018. Silverlake, on the other hand, began at 2.5 million but fell to a low of 1.5 million in 2014. It then recovered slightly to 1.7 million in 2018 and ended the period at 1.6 million.

mistakes.bad: In 2002 it was 1.2 million, in 2006 it was 1.4 million, in 2010 it was 1.7 million and in 2014 it was 2.6 million.

why.en: Listing every point retells the data instead of selecting key features, and Task Achievement drops. Use the start, the turning point, the peak and the end.
why.kk: Барлық нүктені қатарынан беру — басты нәрсені іріктеу емес, жай қайталау: Task Achievement төмендейді. Басын, бетбұрысын, шыңы мен соңын алыңыз.
why.ru: Все точки подряд — пересказ, а не отбор главного: Task Achievement снижается. Берите начало, перелом, пик и конец.

mistakes.good: Visitor numbers at Redrock rose steadily from 1.2 million in 2002 to 1.7 million in 2010 and then climbed sharply.

mistakes.bad: Overall, Redrock increased from 1.2 million to 4.2 million visitors.

why.en: An overview with figures is just another detail. Name the trend in words and keep the figures for the next paragraphs.
why.kk: Сандары бар overview — тағы бір толық дерек қана. Үрдісті сөзбен атаңыз, сандар — келесі абзацтарда.
why.ru: Overview с цифрами — это ещё одна деталь. Назовите тенденцию словами, цифры — в следующих абзацах.

mistakes.good: Overall, Redrock saw a dramatic increase and became the most visited park.

mistakes.bad: The number of visitors to Redrock rose on 3 million.

why.en: The difference takes by, the end point takes to: rose by 3 million, rose to 4.2 million. “Rose on” is a word-for-word translation from Russian or Kazakh.
why.kk: Айырма — by, нәтиже — to: rose by 3 million, rose to 4.2 million. «Rose on» — «3 миллионға өсті» тіркесінің сөзбе-сөз аудармасы.
why.ru: Разница — by, итог — to: rose by 3 million, rose to 4.2 million. «Rose on» — калька с «выросло на».

mistakes.good: The number of visitors to Redrock rose by 3 million.

mistakes.bad: Cycling in Northport rose by 2% between 2004 and 2008.

why.en: A difference between percentages is measured in percentage points. “By 2%” means 2% of the starting value: from 5% to 5.1%.
why.kk: Пайыздар арасындағы айырма — percentage points. «By 2%» дегені — бастапқы мәннің 2 %-ы: 5 %-дан 5,1 %-ға дейін.
why.ru: Разница между процентами — percentage points. «By 2%» значит «на 2 % от исходного»: с 5 % до 5,1 %.

mistakes.good: Cycling in Northport rose by 2 percentage points, from 5% to 7%.

mistakes.bad: Visitor numbers increase sharply after 2010.

why.en: Past years take the past simple. After by 2022 use the past perfect: had reached. Forecasts for future years take is expected to / is predicted to.
why.kk: Өткен жылдар — past simple. by 2022 тіркесінен кейін — past perfect: had reached. Келешек жылдарға болжам — is expected to / is predicted to.
why.ru: Прошедшие годы — past simple. После by 2022 — past perfect: had reached. Прогноз на будущие годы — is expected to / is predicted to.

mistakes.good: Visitor numbers increased sharply after 2010.

mistakes.bad: Redrock became popular because a new road was built.

why.en: The graph shows no reasons. An invented explanation is irrelevant information and lowers Task Achievement.
why.kk: Графикте себеп жоқ. Ойдан шығарылған түсіндірме — артық ақпарат, Task Achievement төмендейді.
why.ru: Причин на графике нет. Выдуманное объяснение — лишняя информация, Task Achievement снижается.

mistakes.good: Redrock had become the most visited park by 2018.

mistakes.bad: The amount of visitors to Pinewood stayed the same.

why.en: amount goes with uncountable nouns (amount of money, water). People and objects take number.
why.kk: amount — саналмайтын зат есімге қолданылады (amount of money, water). Адамдар мен заттар — number.
why.ru: amount — для неисчисляемого (amount of money, water). Люди и предметы — number.

mistakes.good: The number of visitors to Pinewood remained broadly stable.

mistakes.bad: The graph below shows the number of visitors to three national parks in one country between 2002 and 2022.

why.en: Words copied from the task do not count towards the word total and show no vocabulary. Change both the words and the structure.
why.kk: Тапсырмадан көшірілген сөздер көлемге есептелмейді және лексиканы көрсетпейді. Сөзді де, құрылымды да өзгертіңіз.
why.ru: Слова, переписанные из задания, не засчитываются в объём и не показывают лексику. Меняйте и слова, и конструкцию.

mistakes.good: The line graph illustrates how many people visited three national parks over a twenty-year period.

skeleton.ex: The line graph illustrates how many people visited three national parks, Redrock, Pinewood and Silverlake, over a twenty-year period from 2002 to 2022.

what.en: Paraphrase the task: type of visual + what is measured + where + period. Do not copy the wording: shows → illustrates, the number of visitors → how many people visited, between 2002 and 2022 → over a twenty-year period from 2002 to 2022.
what.kk: Тапсырманы басқаша айтыңыз: график түрі + не өлшенеді + қай жерде + кезең. Тапсырма сөздерін көшірмеңіз: shows → illustrates, the number of visitors → how many people visited, between 2002 and 2022 → over a twenty-year period from 2002 to 2022.
what.ru: Перефразируйте задание: вид графика + что измеряют + где + период. Не копируйте формулировку: shows → illustrates, the number of visitors → how many people visited, between 2002 and 2022 → over a twenty-year period from 2002 to 2022.

skeleton.ex: Overall, Redrock saw a dramatic increase in visitor numbers and went from being the least visited park to the most popular one.

what.en: Two main trends without figures: which line changed most and in which direction, and what happened to the others. A crossing of lines — if it changes the leader.
what.kk: Сандарсыз екі негізгі үрдіс: қай сызық ең көп және қай бағытта өзгерді, қалғандарында не болды. Сызықтардың қиылысуы — егер соның салдарынан көшбасшы ауысса.
what.ru: Две главные тенденции без цифр: какая линия изменилась сильнее всех и в какую сторону, что с остальными. Пересечение линий — если из-за него сменился лидер.

skeleton.ex: This number rose steadily to 1.7 million in 2010, overtaking Silverlake, and then climbed sharply, reaching 4.2 million by 2022.

what.en: The most striking line: start → turning point → peak or end, with figures and years. One calculated comparison: “three and a half times”.
what.kk: Ең айқын сызық: басы → бетбұрыс → шыңы немесе соңы, сандары мен жылдарымен. Есептелген бір салыстыру: «three and a half times».
what.ru: Самая заметная линия: начало → перелом → пик или конец, с цифрами и годами. Одно сравнение с расчётом: «в три с половиной раза».

skeleton.ex: Pinewood, meanwhile, was the most visited park for most of the period, with numbers fluctuating slightly around 3 million.

what.en: The remaining lines together: compare them with each other and with the first one. Start the paragraph with a linking phrase: meanwhile, on the other hand.
what.kk: Қалған сызықтар бірге: оларды бір-бірімен және біріншісімен салыстырыңыз. Абзац басында — өту сөзі: meanwhile, on the other hand.
what.ru: Остальные линии вместе: сравните их друг с другом и с первой. В начале абзаца — связка-переход: meanwhile, on the other hand.

text: The bar chart compares the average weekly time that people between the ages of 16 and 24 devoted to four leisure activities in 2012 and 2022.
Overall, social media replaced television as the most time-consuming activity over the decade, while time spent reading fell. The figure for sport was the only one that did not change.
In 2012, watching TV took up by far the most time, at 12 hours a week, which was twice as much as the 6 hours spent on social media. Young people spent 5 hours on sport and only 4 hours reading.

By 2022, the picture had changed considerably. Time on social media had more than doubled to 14 hours, whereas TV viewing had dropped to 5 hours, less than half of its 2012 level. Reading also halved, falling to just 2 hours, the lowest figure in the chart. Sport, meanwhile, remained at 5 hours in both years.

chart.title: Weekly hours spent on leisure activities, ages 16–24

sample.title: Young people’s leisure time
sample.question:
The chart below shows how many hours per week young people aged 16 to 24 in one country spent on four leisure activities in 2012 and 2022.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

rows.ex: The bar chart compares the average weekly time that people between the ages of 16 and 24 devoted to four leisure activities in 2012 and 2022.
rows.pattern: The bar chart compares the average [weekly time / number of …] that [who] devoted to [how many categories] in [year] and [year].

rows.ex: Overall, social media replaced television as the most time-consuming activity over the decade, while time spent reading fell.
rows.pattern: Overall, [A] replaced [B] as the most [time-consuming / popular] [activity] over the [decade / period], while [C] fell.

rows.ex: The figure for sport was the only one that did not change.
rows.pattern: The figure for [D] was the only one that did not change.

rows.ex: In 2012, watching TV took up by far the most time, at 12 hours a week, which was twice as much as the 6 hours spent on social media.
rows.pattern: In [year], [A] took up by far the most [time], at [figure], which was twice as much as the [figure] spent on [B].

rows.ex: Young people spent 5 hours on sport and only 4 hours reading.
rows.pattern: [Who] spent [figure] on [C] and only [figure] [doing D].

rows.ex: By 2022, the picture had changed considerably.
rows.pattern: By [year], the picture had changed considerably.

rows.ex: Time on social media had more than doubled to 14 hours, whereas TV viewing had dropped to 5 hours, less than half of its 2012 level.
rows.pattern: [A] had more than doubled to [figure], whereas [B] had dropped to [figure], less than half of its [year] level.

rows.ex: Reading also halved, falling to just 2 hours, the lowest figure in the chart.
rows.pattern: [C] also halved, falling to just [figure], the lowest figure in the chart.

rows.ex: Sport, meanwhile, remained at 5 hours in both years.
rows.pattern: [D], meanwhile, remained at [figure] in both years.

mistakes.bad: TV was 12 hours. Social media was 6 hours. Sport was 5 hours. Reading was 4 hours.

why.en: A row of figures without comparisons is not a description. Start with the largest value and compare: twice as much as, far more than.
why.kk: Салыстыруы жоқ сандар тізбегі сипаттама емес. Ең үлкенінен бастап, салыстырыңыз: twice as much as, far more than.
why.ru: Ряд цифр без сравнения — не описание. Начните с самого большого и сравнивайте: twice as much as, far more than.

mistakes.good: Watching TV took up by far the most time, at 12 hours a week, twice as much as social media.

mistakes.bad: In 2012, sport increased to 5 hours compared with reading.

why.en: Within one year nothing rises or falls — these are different categories. Trend verbs are only for change between years; categories are compared: more … than.
why.kk: Бір жылдың ішінде ештеңе өспейді де, төмендемейді де — бұлар әртүрлі санаттар. Динамика етістіктері тек жылдар арасындағы өзгеріске керек, санаттар салыстырылады: more … than.
why.ru: Внутри одного года ничего не растёт и не падает — это разные категории. Глаголы динамики — только для изменения между годами, категории сравнивают: more … than.

mistakes.good: In 2012, young people spent slightly more time on sport (5 hours) than on reading (4 hours).

mistakes.bad: In 2022, social media took three times more time than TV.

why.en: “Three times more” is a disputed direct translation. The safe form is three times as much / as many as. 14 and 5 make almost three times.
why.kk: «Үш есе көп» → three times more — даулы калька. Сенімді нұсқа: three times as much / as many as. 14 бен 5 — almost three times.
why.ru: «В три раза больше» → three times more — спорная калька. Надёжная форма: three times as much / as many as. 14 и 5 — это almost three times.

mistakes.good: In 2022, young people spent almost three times as much time on social media as on TV.

mistakes.bad: Social media was more higher than TV.

why.en: A double comparative (more higher) is a grammar error. Intensify with much, far, considerably. Compare like with like: the figure for A — that for B.
why.kk: Қос салыстыру (more higher) — грамматикалық қате. Күшейту — much, far, considerably. Біртектес нәрсені салыстырыңыз: the figure for A — that for B.
why.ru: Двойное сравнение (more higher) — грамматическая ошибка. Усиление — much, far, considerably. Сравнивайте однородное: the figure for A — that for B.

mistakes.good: The figure for social media was much higher than that for TV.

mistakes.bad: Young people spent 14 on social media in 2022.

why.en: A figure without a unit is inaccurate data. Check the axis: hours, %, thousands, millions.
why.kk: Өлшем бірлігі жоқ сан — дәл емес дерек. Осьті тексеріңіз: hours, %, thousands, millions.
why.ru: Число без единицы измерения — неточные данные. Проверьте ось: hours, %, thousands, millions.

mistakes.good: Young people spent 14 hours a week on social media in 2022.

mistakes.bad: Overall, TV was 12 hours in 2012 and 5 hours in 2022.

why.en: An overview with figures is just another detail. Name the main change in words.
why.kk: Сандары бар overview — тағы бір толық дерек қана. Басты өзгерісті сөзбен атаңыз.
why.ru: Overview с цифрами — ещё одна деталь. Назовите главное изменение словами.

mistakes.good: Overall, social media replaced television as the most time-consuming activity.

skeleton.ex: The bar chart compares the average weekly time that people between the ages of 16 and 24 devoted to four leisure activities in 2012 and 2022.

what.en: Paraphrase: type of visual + what is measured + who + categories + years. how many hours per week → the average weekly time, aged 16 to 24 → between the ages of 16 and 24, spent on → devoted to.
what.kk: Басқаша айтыңыз: график түрі + не өлшенеді + кім + санаттар + жылдар. how many hours per week → the average weekly time, aged 16 to 24 → between the ages of 16 and 24, spent on → devoted to.
what.ru: Перефразируйте: вид графика + что измеряют + кто + категории + годы. how many hours per week → the average weekly time, aged 16 to 24 → between the ages of 16 and 24, spent on → devoted to.

skeleton.ex: Overall, social media replaced television as the most time-consuming activity over the decade, while time spent reading fell.

what.en: No figures: the largest category and the main change between the years; anything that did not change — if it stands out.
what.kk: Сандарсыз: ең үлкен санат және жылдар арасындағы басты өзгеріс; өзгермеген санат — егер ол көзге түссе.
what.ru: Без цифр: самая большая категория и главное изменение между годами; что не изменилось — если это заметно.

skeleton.ex: In 2012, watching TV took up by far the most time, at 12 hours a week, which was twice as much as the 6 hours spent on social media.

what.en: The first year: categories from largest to smallest, with figures. One “how many times” comparison: twice as much as.
what.kk: Бірінші жыл: санаттар үлкенінен кішісіне қарай, сандарымен. «Неше есе» деген бір салыстыру: twice as much as.
what.ru: Первый год: категории от большей к меньшей, с цифрами. Одно сравнение «во сколько раз»: twice as much as.

skeleton.ex: Time on social media had more than doubled to 14 hours, whereas TV viewing had dropped to 5 hours, less than half of its 2012 level.

what.en: The second year: what changed compared with the first, with figures (past perfect after by 2022). Group by year or by category — whichever gives fewer repetitions.
what.kk: Екінші жыл: біріншімен салыстырғанда не өзгерді, сандарымен (by 2022 тіркесінен кейін — past perfect). Жыл немесе санат бойынша топтаңыз — қайсысында қайталау азырақ болса, соны таңдаңыз.
what.ru: Второй год: что изменилось по сравнению с первым, с цифрами (после by 2022 — past perfect). Группируйте по году или по категории — как получается меньше повторов.

text: The pie charts compare the proportions of electricity that one country generated from five different sources in 2005 and 2025.

Overall, coal remained the largest source of electricity in both years, but its dominance weakened considerably. The most striking change was the rapid growth of wind and solar power, which rose from almost nothing to the third most important source.

In 2005, coal accounted for 62% of all electricity, well over half of the total. Gas was a distant second at 21%, followed by hydropower at 12%. Wind and solar generated just 1%, while other sources made up the remaining 4%.

Twenty years later, the share of coal had fallen to 41%, although it was still the largest single source by a wide margin. Gas rose to 27%, whereas hydropower stayed almost unchanged at 11%. Wind and solar, meanwhile, increased sixteenfold to 16%, overtaking hydropower. The figure for other sources edged up to 5%.
sample.title: Sources of electricity
sample.question:
The pie charts below show where one country’s electricity came from in 2005 and 2025.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

rows.ex: The pie charts compare the proportions of electricity that one country generated from five different sources in 2005 and 2025.
rows.pattern: The pie charts compare the proportions of [what] that [who] [generated / spent] from [how many] different [sources] in [year] and [year].

rows.ex: Overall, coal remained the largest source of electricity in both years, but its dominance weakened considerably.
rows.pattern: Overall, [A] remained the largest [source] in both years, but its dominance weakened considerably.

rows.ex: The most striking change was the rapid growth of wind and solar power, which rose from almost nothing to the third most important source.
rows.pattern: The most striking change was the rapid growth of [B], which rose from almost nothing to [its new position].

rows.ex: In 2005, coal accounted for 62% of all electricity, well over half of the total.
rows.pattern: In [year], [A] accounted for [figure] of all [what], well over half of the total.

rows.ex: Gas was a distant second at 21%, followed by hydropower at 12%.
rows.pattern: [B] was a distant second at [figure], followed by [C] at [figure].

rows.ex: Wind and solar generated just 1%, while other sources made up the remaining 4%.
rows.pattern: [D] [generated] just [figure], while [other sources] made up the remaining [figure].

rows.ex: Twenty years later, the share of coal had fallen to 41%, although it was still the largest single source
rows.pattern: [Twenty] years later, the share of [A] had fallen to [figure], although it was still the largest single [source].

rows.ex: Gas rose to 27%, whereas hydropower stayed almost unchanged at 11%.
rows.pattern: [B] rose to [figure], whereas [C] stayed almost unchanged at [figure].

rows.ex: Wind and solar, meanwhile, increased sixteenfold to 16%, overtaking hydropower.
rows.pattern: [D], meanwhile, increased [sixteenfold] to [figure], overtaking [C].

rows.ex: The figure for other sources edged up to 5%.
rows.pattern: The figure for [E] edged up to [figure].

mistakes.bad: The percent of coal was 62%.

why.en: percent only follows a number. Before of use proportion, share or percentage.
why.kk: percent — тек саннан кейін. of алдында — proportion, share, percentage.
why.ru: percent — только после числа. Перед of — proportion, share, percentage.

mistakes.good: The proportion of electricity generated from coal was 62%.

mistakes.bad: The country produced more electricity from gas in 2025.

why.en: A pie chart shows shares, not amounts. A larger share does not mean a larger quantity.
why.kk: Дөңгелек диаграмма көлемді емес, үлесті көрсетеді. Үлестің өсуі мөлшердің өсуі дегенді білдірмейді.
why.ru: Круговая диаграмма показывает доли, а не объём. Доля выросла — не значит, что выросло количество.

mistakes.good: Gas accounted for a larger share of electricity in 2025.

mistakes.bad: Wind and solar rose by 15%.

why.en: A change in share is measured in percentage points. “By 15%” would mean 15% of 1%.

text: The table illustrates how common five electronic devices were in households in one country at ten-year intervals from 2004 to 2024.

Overall, ownership of every device except the desktop computer increased over the period. Smartphones saw the most dramatic change, becoming almost universal, while desktop computers went from being the most widely owned device to the least common.

In 2004, 58% of households had a desktop computer, compared with only 22% that owned a laptop, making it by far the most popular device. Smartphones were rare, at just 3%, and tablets and smart TVs did not appear in any homes.

By 2024, the picture had reversed. Smartphone ownership had soared to 96%, and laptops had become the second most common device, at 72%. Smart TVs rose rapidly from 12% in 2014 to 58%, while tablets grew more slowly, reaching 45%. In contrast, the proportion of homes with a desktop computer fell steadily to 21%, less than half of its 2004 level.

text: The diagram illustrates the process by which used cooking oil is turned into biodiesel, a fuel for vehicles.

Overall, the process consists of nine stages, beginning with the collection of waste oil from restaurants and ending with the delivery of fuel to petrol stations. It is largely a chemical process, and it also produces glycerine as a by-product.

First, used oil is collected from restaurants and transported to a processing plant by tanker. There, it is filtered to remove food particles and then heated to 60°C. After that, the warm oil is mixed with methanol and a catalyst, which starts a chemical reaction.

Next, the mixture is left to settle for eight hours, during which time it separates into two layers. The heavier layer, glycerine, is drained off and sold to soap manufacturers, while the remaining biodiesel is washed and dried. Finally, the fuel is stored in tanks before being delivered to petrol stations.

text: The two maps illustrate how a riverside district of a town was transformed over a twenty-year period from 2005 to 2025.

Overall, the area changed from an industrial zone dominated by traffic into a residential and leisure space. The most noticeable developments were the removal of the factory and the closure of the main road to cars.

In 2005, a large factory occupied the north-western part of the area, to the west of a main road which ran from north to south and crossed the river by a road bridge. To the east of the road, there was a car park, and a warehouse stood on the northern bank of the river.

By 2025, the factory had been demolished and replaced with apartment blocks, and a few small shops had opened beside the street. The road itself had been pedestrianised, while the car park had been converted into a park with a playground. The warehouse had made way for a café with a terrace. In addition, a footbridge had been built to the east of the road bridge, and trees had been planted along the riverbank.

sample.title: A riverside district
sample.question:
The maps below show a riverside area of a town in 2005 and in 2025.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

rows.ex: The two maps illustrate how a riverside district of a town was transformed over a twenty-year period from 2005 to 2025.
rows.pattern: The two maps illustrate how [place] was transformed over a [twenty]-year period from [year] to [year].

rows.ex: Overall, the area changed from an industrial zone dominated by traffic into a residential and leisure space.
rows.pattern: Overall, the area changed from [what it was] into [what it became].

rows.ex: The most noticeable developments were the removal of the factory and the closure of the main road to cars.
rows.pattern: The most noticeable developments were [change 1] and [change 2].

rows.ex: In 2005, a large factory occupied the north-western part of the area, to the west of a main road
rows.pattern: In [year], [a large factory] occupied the [north-western] part of the area, to the west of [landmark].

rows.ex: ran from north to south and crossed the river by a road bridge
rows.pattern: [A road] ran from [north] to [south] and crossed the river by [a road bridge].

rows.ex: To the east of the road, there was a car park, and a warehouse stood on the northern bank of the river.
rows.pattern: To the east of [landmark], there was [feature], and [feature] stood on the [northern] bank of the river.

rows.ex: By 2025, the factory had been demolished and replaced with apartment blocks
rows.pattern: By [year], [A] had been demolished and replaced with [B].

rows.ex: the car park had been converted into a park with a playground
rows.pattern: [C] had been converted into [D].

rows.ex: The warehouse had made way for a café with a terrace.
rows.pattern: [E] had made way for [F].

rows.ex: In addition, a footbridge had been built to the east of the road bridge, and trees had been planted along the riverbank.
rows.pattern: In addition, [new feature] had been built to the [east] of [landmark], and [trees] had been planted along [where].

mistakes.bad: The factory was on the north-west of the area.

why.en: Inside the area — in the north-west; outside it — to the north-west of; on the edge — on the northern bank.
why.kk: Аумақтың ішінде — in the north-west; сыртында — to the north-west of; шекарасында — on the northern bank.
why.ru: Внутри области — in the north-west; за её пределами — to the north-west of; на границе — on the northern bank.

mistakes.good: A large factory occupied the north-western part of the area.

mistakes.bad: By 2025, the factory demolished.

why.en: A building does not demolish itself — use the passive. “By 2025” needs the past perfect: had been demolished.
why.kk: Ғимарат өзін-өзі бұзбайды — passive. «By 2025» past perfect-ті талап етеді: had been demolished.
why.ru: Здание не сносит само себя — passive. «By 2025» требует past perfect: had been demolished.

mistakes.good: By 2025, the factory had been demolished.

mistakes.bad: The car park changed to a park.

why.en: Use a precise verb of change: converted into, replaced with, made way for, extended, relocated.
why.kk: Өзгерістің дәл етістігі: converted into, replaced with, made way for, extended, relocated.
why.ru: Точный глагол перемены: converted into, replaced with, made way for, extended, relocated.

mistakes.good: The car park had been converted into a park with a playground.

mistakes.bad: In 2005, there is a factory in the north-west.

why.en: A map of a past year takes the past simple; the present is only for a “now” map or a future plan.
why.kk: Өткен жылдың картасы — past simple; осы шақ тек «қазір» картасына немесе болашақ жоспарына.
why.ru: Карта прошлого года — past simple; настоящее время только для карты «сейчас» или плана на будущее.

mistakes.good: In 2005, a large factory occupied the north-western part of the area.

mistakes.bad: The factory was closed because residents complained about pollution.

why.en: Maps show no reasons — only what was where and what changed.
why.kk: Картада себеп жоқ — тек не қайда болғаны және не өзгергені.
why.ru: Причин на карте нет — только что где было и что изменилось.

mistakes.good: The factory had been demolished and replaced with apartment blocks.

skeleton.ex: The two maps illustrate how a riverside district of a town was transformed over a twenty-year period from 2005 to 2025.

what.en: Paraphrase: maps + which place + years. show a riverside area in 2005 and in 2025 → illustrate how a riverside district was transformed from 2005 to 2025.
what.kk: Басқаша айтыңыз: maps + қай жер + жылдар. show a riverside area in 2005 and in 2025 → illustrate how a riverside district was transformed from 2005 to 2025.
what.ru: Перефразируйте: maps + какое место + годы. show a riverside area in 2005 and in 2025 → illustrate how a riverside district was transformed from 2005 to 2025.

skeleton.ex: Overall, the area changed from an industrial zone dominated by traffic into a residential and leisure space.

what.en: The general character of the change (industrial → residential, more or less green space) and the 1–2 biggest changes. No small details.
what.kk: Өзгерістердің жалпы сипаты (өндірістік → тұрғын, жасыл аймақ көбейді / азайды) және 1–2 ең ірі өзгеріс. Ұсақ-түйексіз.
what.ru: Общий характер перемен (промышленный → жилой, больше / меньше зелени) и 1–2 самых крупных изменения. Без мелочей.

skeleton.ex: In 2005, a large factory occupied the north-western part of the area

what.en: The first map: what was where, with locations (in the north-west, to the east of, on the northern bank). Past simple.
what.kk: Бірінші карта: не қайда болды — орнын көрсетіп (in the north-west, to the east of, on the northern bank). Past simple.
what.ru: Первая карта: что где было — с указанием места (in the north-west, to the east of, on the northern bank). Past simple.

skeleton.ex: By 2025, the factory had been demolished and replaced with apartment blocks

what.en: The second map through changes: passive and past perfect (had been demolished, had been converted into); new things — had been built.
what.kk: Екінші карта — өзгерістер арқылы: passive және past perfect (had been demolished, had been converted into); жаңасы — had been built.
what.ru: Вторая карта через изменения: passive и past perfect (had been demolished, had been converted into); новое — had been built.

text: The charts give information about international tourism in one country: the bar chart illustrates how many foreign visitors arrived every two years from 2016 to 2024, and the pie chart breaks down their reasons for travelling in 2024.
Overall, visitor numbers rose over the period apart from one dramatic fall, and at the end of the period they reached their highest level. Holidays were by far the most common reason for visiting.

In 2016, the country received 4.1 million visitors, and this figure grew to 5 million two years later. In 2020, however, the number collapsed to just 1.2 million, less than a quarter of the previous level. It then recovered strongly to 4.6 million in 2022 and peaked at 6.3 million in 2024.

Turning to the purposes of visits in 2024, almost half of all tourists (48%) came on holiday. Business travel accounted for 22%, slightly more than the 18% who were visiting friends and family. Only 7% travelled to study, and the remaining 5% came for other reasons.
sample.title: International visitors
sample.question:
The bar chart below shows the number of international visitors to one country between 2016 and 2024. The pie chart shows the main purposes of their visits in 2024.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

rows.ex: The charts give information about international tourism in one country: the bar chart illustrates how many foreign visitors arrived every two years from 2016 to 2024, and the pie chart breaks down their reasons for travelling in 2024.
rows.pattern: The charts give information about [topic]: the [bar chart] illustrates [what], and the [pie chart] breaks down [what].

rows.ex: Overall, visitor numbers rose over the period apart from one dramatic fall, and at the end of the period they reached their highest level.
rows.pattern: Overall, [figures] rose over the period apart from [exception], and at the end of the period they reached their highest level.

rows.ex: Holidays were by far the most common reason for visiting.
rows.pattern: [A] were by far the most common [reason].

rows.ex: In 2016, the country received 4.1 million visitors, and this figure grew to 5 million two years later.
rows.pattern: In [year], [the country] received [figure] [visitors], and this figure grew to [figure] [two years later].

rows.ex: In 2020, however, the number collapsed to just 1.2 million, less than a quarter of the previous level.
rows.pattern: In [year], however, the number collapsed to just [figure], less than a quarter of the previous level.

rows.ex: It then recovered strongly to 4.6 million in 2022 and peaked at 6.3 million in 2024.
rows.pattern: It then recovered strongly to [figure] in [year] and peaked at [figure] in [year].

rows.ex: Turning to the purposes of visits in 2024, almost half of all tourists (48%) came on holiday.
rows.pattern: Turning to [the second chart’s topic], almost half of all [people] ([figure]) [did what].

rows.ex: Business travel accounted for 22%, slightly more than the 18% who were visiting friends and family.
rows.pattern: [B] accounted for [figure], slightly more than the [figure] who [did what].

rows.ex: Only 7% travelled to study, and the remaining 5% came for other reasons.
rows.pattern: Only [figure] [did what], and the remaining [figure] [did what].

mistakes.bad: Overall, visitor numbers rose, and in 2020 they fell to 1.2 million.

why.en: The overview needs one main feature from each chart, without figures. An overview of one chart only is incomplete.
why.kk: Overview — әр графиктің басты белгісі, сандарсыз. Бір графиктің overview-і — толық емес.
why.ru: Overview — по главной черте с каждого графика и без цифр. Overview по одному графику — неполный.

mistakes.good: Overall, visitor numbers rose over the period apart from one dramatic fall. Holidays were by far the most common reason for visiting.

mistakes.bad: Visitor numbers rose because more people came on holiday.

why.en: The charts do not show why numbers rose. Link them only where the data shows a link.
why.kk: Графиктер өсудің себебін көрсетпейді. Олардың байланысы — деректе көрінсе ғана.
why.ru: Графики не показывают причину роста. Связь между ними — только если она видна в данных.

mistakes.good: Holidays were by far the most common reason for visiting.

mistakes.bad: In 2024, 48 million tourists came on holiday.

why.en: Each chart has its own units: millions in the bar chart, percentages in the pie chart. Do not mix them.
why.kk: Әр графиктің өз өлшем бірлігі бар: bar-да — миллион, pie-да — пайыз. Араластырмаңыз.
why.ru: У каждого графика свои единицы: в bar — миллионы, в pie — проценты. Не смешивайте.

mistakes.good: In 2024, almost half of all tourists (48%) came on holiday.

mistakes.bad: The bar chart shows visitors. The pie chart shows purposes.

why.en: The introduction is one sentence about both charts and their shared topic, not two short ones.
why.kk: Кіріспе — екі қысқа сөйлем емес, екі график пен ортақ тақырып туралы бір сөйлем.
why.ru: Вступление — одно предложение про оба графика и общую тему, а не два коротких.

mistakes.good: The charts give information about international tourism in one country: the bar chart illustrates how many foreign visitors arrived, and the pie chart breaks down their reasons for travelling.

mistakes.bad: (the pie chart is described in one sentence at the end)

why.en: The second chart gets its own paragraph of equal weight; a skipped or rushed chart lowers Task Achievement.
why.kk: Екінші график — салмағы бірдей жеке абзац; жіберілген немесе тым қысқа график Task Achievement-ті төмендетеді.
why.ru: Второй график — отдельный абзац того же веса; пропущенный или скомканный график снижает Task Achievement.

mistakes.good: Turning to the purposes of visits in 2024, almost half of all tourists (48%) came on holiday.

skeleton.ex: the bar chart illustrates how many foreign visitors arrived every two years from 2016 to 2024, and the pie chart breaks down their reasons for travelling in 2024

what.en: Both charts in one sentence: what each one shows. A colon or and links them.
what.kk: Екі график бір сөйлемде: әрқайсысы нені көрсетеді. Қос нүкте немесе and оларды байланыстырады.
what.ru: Оба графика в одном предложении: что показывает каждый. Двоеточие или and связывают их.

skeleton.ex: Holidays were by far the most common reason for visiting.

what.en: One main feature from each chart. A link between the charts only if the data shows it.
what.kk: Әр графиктен бір басты белгі. Графиктер арасындағы байланыс — деректе көрінсе ғана.
what.ru: По одной главной черте с каждого графика. Связь между графиками — только если она видна в данных.

skeleton.ex: In 2016, the country received 4.1 million visitors, and this figure grew to 5 million two years later.

what.en: The first chart in full — with its own units (millions).
what.kk: Бірінші график толық — өз өлшем бірлігімен (millions).
what.ru: Первый график целиком — со своими единицами (millions).

skeleton.ex: Turning to the purposes of visits in 2024, almost half of all tourists (48%) came on holiday.

what.en: The second chart — with a transition (Turning to…) and its own units (%).
what.kk: Екінші график — өту сөзімен (Turning to…) және өз өлшем бірлігімен (%).
what.ru: Второй график — с переходом (Turning to…) и своими единицами (%).

rules.en: Four paragraphs: introduction, overview and two detail paragraphs. No conclusion is needed — the overview does that job.
rules.kk: Төрт абзац: кіріспе, overview және толығырақ екі абзац. Қорытынды (conclusion) керек емес — оның рөлін overview атқарады.
rules.ru: Четыре абзаца: вступление, overview и два абзаца деталей. Вывод (conclusion) не нужен — его роль играет overview.

rules.en: The overview is compulsory and has no figures: without it Task Achievement cannot go above 5.
rules.kk: Overview міндетті және сандарсыз беріледі: онсыз Task Achievement 5-тен аспайды.
rules.ru: Overview обязателен и без цифр: без него Task Achievement не выше 5.

rules.en: Choose figures selectively: start, end, peaks, crossings, the largest and the smallest. Listing every point is a mistake.
rules.kk: Сандар іріктеліп беріледі: басы, соңы, шыңдары, қиылысулар, ең үлкені мен ең кішісі. Барлық нүктені қатарынан беру — қате.
rules.ru: Цифры — выборочно: начало, конец, пики, пересечения, самое большое и самое маленькое. Все точки подряд — ошибка.

rules.en: Only what the visual shows: no reasons, predictions or opinions.
rules.kk: Тек суретте бар дерек: себеп, болжам және жеке пікір болмайды.
rules.ru: Только то, что на картинке: без причин, прогнозов и своего мнения.

rules.en: 150–190 words. A longer answer does not score higher — it only leaves more room for mistakes.
rules.kk: 150–190 сөз. Ұзын жауап баллды көтермейді, тек қатеге орын көбейеді.
rules.ru: 150–190 слов. Длиннее — балл не выше, а места для ошибок больше.

rules.en: The same verb again and again is the clearest sign of a weak Task 1. Alternate verb + adverb (rose sharply) with adjective + noun (a sharp rise).
rules.kk: Бір етістікті қатарынан қолдану — әлсіз Task 1-дің басты белгісі. Үстеулі етістік (rose sharply) пен сын есімді зат есімді (a sharp rise) алмастырып отырыңыз.
rules.ru: Один и тот же глагол подряд — главный признак слабого Task 1. Чередуйте глагол с наречием (rose sharply) и существительное с прилагательным (a sharp rise).

rules.en: The strength of the word must match the chart: 4 → 7 is not soared; 3 → 96 is not rose slightly.
rules.kk: Сөздің күші графикке сай болуы керек: 4 → 7 — soared емес, 3 → 96 — rose slightly емес.
rules.ru: Сила слова должна совпадать с графиком: 4 → 7 — не soared, 3 → 96 — не rose slightly.

rules.en: The difference takes by, the end point to, the start from, a level at. A wrong preposition changes the figure.
rules.kk: Айырма — by, нәтиже — to, бастауы — from, деңгей — at. Предлог қатесі санды өзгертеді.
rules.ru: Разница — by, итог — to, начало — from, уровень — at. Ошибка в предлоге меняет цифру.

rules.en: Examples come from our model answers; the “Worked example” chip opens the full answer in “Task 1 Academic: templates”.
rules.kk: Мысалдар — біздің үлгі жауаптардан; «Талданған мысал» чипі жауапты «Task 1 Academic: шаблондар» бетінде толық ашады.
rules.ru: Примеры — из наших модельных ответов; чип «Разобранный пример» открывает ответ целиком в «Task 1 Academic: шаблоны».

note.en: The sharpest come first. Task 1 is mostly in the past simple, so the forms are past.
note.kk: Жоғарыда — ең күрттері. Task 1-де бәрі дерлік past simple, сондықтан формалар — өткен шақта.
note.ru: Сверху — самые резкие. В Task 1 почти всё в past simple, поэтому формы — прошедшие.

rows.ex: Smartphone ownership had soared to 96%

text: Dear Mr Collins,
I am writing to apologise about your ladder, which I am afraid was damaged while I was using it last weekend.

I was cleaning the gutters on Saturday afternoon when a strong gust of wind blew the ladder sideways. It fell onto the path, and one of the side rails was badly bent. Fortunately, nobody was hurt, but the ladder is no longer safe to use.
I feel terrible about this, especially as you were kind enough to lend it to me without hesitation. I should have tied it to the drainpipe, as you suggested, and I realise it was my fault.

I would like to replace it with the same model, which I have already found at the hardware shop on Station Road. If you would prefer a different one, or would rather I paid you the cost, please just let me know.
Once again, I am very sorry for the inconvenience. I will drop by on Thursday evening to discuss it, if that suits you.

Kind regards,
Anna Petrova

what.kk: Басты ойды қайталау + келесі қадам.
what.ru: Главное ещё раз + следующий шаг.

skeleton.ex: Kind regards,

what.en: Kind regards, and your first name and surname.
what.kk: Kind regards, және аты-жөні.
what.ru: Kind regards, и имя с фамилией.

text: Dear Sam,
I’ve just got your invitation and I had to write straight away — congratulations to you both!
Thank you so much for inviting me. It means a lot that you want me there on such a special day, especially after all these years.

Unfortunately, I won’t be able to make it. My company is sending me to a conference in Singapore that week, and I found out about it only yesterday, so there’s no way I can get out of it. I’m really gutted to miss it.

How about meeting up when you’re back from your honeymoon? I’ll be in town at the end of June, so maybe we could go to that little Italian place we used to love. My treat, of course! Just let me know which weekend works best for you.
Have a fantastic day, and send my love to Maria. I can’t wait to see the photos!

Lots of love,
Dana
